paragraphs: WENO connects two ways of classifying whole slide pathology images: predicting a label for an entire collection of image instances, and predicting labels for individual instances. The setting is weakly supervised, meaning the available labels describe the whole collection rather than each member. The paper uses knowledge distillation to let the two classifiers help one another.

An attention-based collection classifier serves as the teacher. Its normalized attention scores provide soft training targets for instances belonging to positive collections. The instance classifier learns from these targets, and both models share an instance feature extractor. This shared component gives their learning processes another route to exchange information.

The information flow also runs back toward the teacher. Predictions from the instance classifier guide a strategy for finding difficult positive instances, encouraging the teacher to continue identifying them. WENO is designed to attach to existing attention-based collection classifiers. Experiments on five datasets support the framework’s efficiency, with the central contribution being mutual improvement through weak supervision at two levels.
neurips-2022-bi-directional-weakly-super.tldr: WENO links slide-level and instance-level classifiers so that each helps train the other using weak labels.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation assigns categories across an image, making differences between training and deployment imagery especially consequential. This paper studies unsupervised domain adaptation, where a model must transfer from a source domain to a target domain. Its starting point is that a direct transfer often leaves substantial differences insufficiently aligned.

Deliberated Domain Bridging creates intermediate domains by mixing source and target data at two levels of granularity. One path uses coarse mixing and the other uses fine mixing. Models trained on these two intermediate domains act as complementary teachers. A student then learns from both through cross-path knowledge distillation, bringing together information obtained along the two routes.

The method alternates between constructing these bridges and transferring knowledge across them. The intended benefit is a reinforcing process: intermediate training connects the domains, while distillation combines the complementary models. Experiments across different adaptive segmentation settings report significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods. These findings support using structured data mixing and multiple teachers to address the domain gap in dense prediction.
neurips-2022-deliberated-domain-bridging.tldr: DDB combines coarse and fine data mixing with alternating multi-teacher distillation to improve domain-adaptive segmentation.

paragraphs: DooD explores whether a model can learn a shared drawing process that transfers across different kinds of images and tasks. Its organizing idea is that characters, numbers, and doodles can all be described as arrangements of pen strokes. Representing those strokes explicitly could provide reusable structure across visual categories.

The model combines neural learning with a symbolic stroke-based generator. It learns directly from images without supervision and uses amortized inference: a learned inference process replaces expensive inference performed separately at test time. The symbolic representation is intended to make the inferred drawing structure easier to interpret while supporting generalization beyond the training distribution.

The authors evaluate transfer across five datasets, including transfers between handwritten digits and drawings, and report clear improvements over the compared baselines. They also test selected Omniglot tasks involving new-example generation and one-shot classification, where DooD matches state-of-the-art performance. Together, these results support the usefulness of stroke representations across the evaluated data and tasks, as a step toward more general concept learning.
neurips-2022-drawing-out-of-distribution.tldr: DooD learns symbolic stroke representations from images that transfer across drawing datasets and support generation and one-shot classification.

paragraphs: DreamShard addresses how to distribute embedding tables across hardware devices in a recommender system. A good placement must balance computation with communication. The problem becomes harder when table operations are fused, because the system must reason about the cost of a combined operation, and when deployments contain different numbers of tables or devices.

The approach uses reinforcement learning supported by a learned cost network. That network predicts fused-operation costs and supplies estimated states and rewards for training the placement policy. This lets policy training proceed in an estimated decision process without real GPU execution. Sum and maximum reductions make the network representations accommodate varying numbers of tables and devices.

The authors state that these representations support direct transfer to unseen placement tasks of different sizes without fine-tuning. Experiments using large synthetic tables and production tables show improvements over human-expert and recurrent-network strategies, reaching up to 19% speedup over the strongest baseline. The result links reusable placement decisions with explicit modeling of fused-operation costs.
neurips-2022-dreamshard-generalizable-em.tldr: DreamShard learns embedding-table placements using predicted execution costs and transfers across different numbers of tables and devices.

paragraphs: A GAN’s discriminator learns to distinguish real examples from generated ones. Although the real-data distribution stays fixed, the generator changes during training, continually changing the discriminator’s task. This paper argues that adjusting the discriminator’s learning capacity during training can help it keep pace with that changing problem.

The proposed strategy, DynamicD, uses different adjustments depending on data availability. With sufficient training data, progressively increasing discriminator capacity is beneficial. With limited data, gradually reducing layer width helps reduce discriminator overfitting. These are distinct responses to different training conditions, rather than one capacity schedule intended for every setting.

The empirical study reports improved synthesis without additional computation cost or extra training objectives. Evaluations cover both ordinary image synthesis and 3D-aware synthesis across multiple datasets, supporting the method’s applicability across those tested settings. DynamicD also yields further gains when combined with augmentation, regularization, and pretraining. Its contribution is therefore a change to how discriminator capacity evolves that can complement other ways of improving discriminator training.
neurips-2022-improving-gans-with-a-dynam.tldr: DynamicD adjusts discriminator capacity during GAN training to improve synthesis under both ample-data and limited-data conditions.

paragraphs: Neural query answering can help reason over incomplete knowledge graphs, but many methods attach learned representations to the particular entities present during training. When new entities appear, those representations need retraining. This paper studies inductive query answering, where queries can involve both familiar and previously unseen entities at inference time.

The authors develop two mechanisms powered by graph neural networks. One uses inductive node representations, while the other represents relational structure. Both approaches aim to make reasoning depend on transferable graph information rather than solely on a fixed inventory of entity embeddings. This changes how a query-answering system can accommodate a growing graph.

Experiments show reasoning over unseen nodes and generalization to graphs reported as up to 500% larger than the training graphs. The two mechanisms offer different efficiency and effectiveness tradeoffs. Relational structure representations generally perform better, while the node-based method can answer complex queries without training on queries and scale to graphs containing millions of nodes. The findings distinguish these capabilities rather than identifying one approach as best in every respect.
neurips-2022-inductive-logical-query-ans.tldr: Two graph-based representation methods enable logical query answering over new entities, with different accuracy and scalability tradeoffs.

paragraphs: LASSIE reconstructs articulated animal shape and pose from a small collection of 10–30 images of one species. The images can show different animal instances, poses, backgrounds, lighting, and textures. The method does not assume predefined template shapes, ground-truth 2D or 3D annotations, or information linking images through multiple views or time.

The approach builds on the observation that individual body parts have simpler shapes than a complete animal and remain useful units as the animal changes pose. Its optimization framework discovers 3D parts through self-supervision with minimal user intervention. A central constraint encourages agreement between 2D and 3D parts using self-supervisory deep features.

This part-based organization gives the reconstruction process structure without requiring a complete animal template in advance. Evaluations on Pascal-Part and collected animal images report considerably better 3D reconstructions and better part discovery in both two and three dimensions than prior approaches. The stated setting is particularly relevant to reconstructing a species from a sparse, varied image collection rather than coordinated captures.
neurips-2022-lassie-learning-articulated.tldr: LASSIE discovers 3D animal parts to reconstruct articulated shapes from 10–30 varied images with minimal user intervention.

paragraphs: This paper studies cooperation among agents arranged in a partially connected network. Each agent interacts and communicates only with nearby agents, yet the group must optimize a global objective. The challenge is to make decentralized decisions serve that collective objective despite the restrictions on who can exchange information.

LToS introduces two levels of policy for each agent. The high-level policy learns how to share reward with neighbors, shaping the local objectives pursued across the network. The low-level policy learns actions that optimize the objective induced by reward-sharing policies in its neighborhood. These policies are trained alternately as a two-level optimization problem.

Reward sharing is therefore something agents learn dynamically, rather than merely a fixed rule supplied before action learning begins. This provides a mechanism for encouraging local cooperation in support of the global goal. Experiments in social dilemmas and networked multi-agent settings across scales show LToS outperforming existing methods. The evidence supports learned reward allocation as a useful component of decentralized cooperation in the evaluated scenarios.
neurips-2022-learning-to-share-in-networ.tldr: LToS learns how neighboring agents share rewards and choose actions to improve decentralized cooperation.

paragraphs: Logical Credal Networks provide a way to combine logical statements with uncertain information expressed as probability bounds. Instead of requiring one exact probability distribution, an LCN describes a collection of distributions consistent with the supplied bounds. These constraints can concern both probabilities of logical formulas and conditional probabilities.

The formalism accommodates propositional and first-order logic with relatively few restrictions, including no requirement that the structure be acyclic. It also introduces a generalized Markov condition for identifying independence relationships between atomic formulas. This gives the framework both a language for expressing uncertain knowledge and a way to capture independence implicit in its structure.

The authors evaluate LCNs on random networks, uncertain Mastermind games, and credit card fraud detection. They report better performance than existing approaches and attribute the advantage to combining multiple sources of imprecise information. The contribution matters when available knowledge constrains probabilities without determining them exactly: the model preserves that imprecision while bringing the constraints together in a common probabilistic logic.
neurips-2022-logical-credal-networks-8c7.tldr: Logical Credal Networks combine logical formulas and probability bounds to reason with multiple sources of imprecise information.

paragraphs: This paper asks how many samples are needed to learn equilibrium behavior in multi-agent Markov games. It focuses on finite-horizon games whose dynamics can vary across time and assumes access to a generative model, a flexible sampling mechanism. That sampling assumption is part of the setting in which its guarantees apply.

The authors introduce Q-FTRL and an adaptive sampling strategy, combining optimistic learning with Follow-the-Regularized-Leader. For general-sum games, the algorithm learns an approximately coarse correlated equilibrium with sample complexity proportional, up to logarithmic factors, to H⁴ times the number of states times the sum of players’ action counts, divided by the squared target error. The dependence uses the sum of action counts rather than their product.

For a fixed number of players, the bound is minimax-optimal up to logarithmic factors. In two-player zero-sum games, the method also has a sample-optimal guarantee for an approximate Nash equilibrium. The analysis additionally refines FTRL’s regret bound to expose the contribution of variance-related quantities.
neurips-2022-minimax-optimal-multi-agent.tldr: With generative-model sampling, Q-FTRL achieves equilibrium-learning sample bounds that are minimax-optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed player counts.

paragraphs: Neural shape representations face a tension between accurate reconstruction and flexible editing. A representation fitted closely to one object can preserve its details but fail when parts move into unfamiliar arrangements. A representation learned across a family of shapes can handle variation, but its reconstruction of a particular object is more approximate.

NeuForm combines these strengths by adapting a generalizable representation where reliable object data is available. Elsewhere, it retains the generalizable representation. A specially designed architecture and a method for blending the two representations’ network weights allow these behaviors to coexist. The intended result is an editable shape that retains the accuracy associated with fitting a particular object.

The authors demonstrate changes to the arrangement of parts in chairs, tables, and lamps while preserving reconstruction accuracy. Comparisons against two state-of-the-art competitors show improvements in both plausibility and fidelity of the edited shapes. These results support selective adaptation as a way to reconcile detailed object reconstruction with the ability to handle new configurations.
neurips-2022-neuform-adaptive-overfittin.tldr: NeuForm blends object-specific fitting with a generalizable shape representation to support edits while preserving detailed geometry.

paragraphs: Set functions assign values to discrete selections, making them useful for many discrete reasoning and optimization problems. Integrating them into neural networks creates two difficulties: discrete choices do not naturally support gradient-based optimization, and their representation can conflict with the high-dimensional vector spaces used in deep learning.

The paper first develops a framework that extends set functions into continuous, low-dimensional domains. This makes it possible to work with continuous counterparts of the discrete functions and includes several established extensions as special cases. The authors then address the representation issue separately, converting those extensions into high-dimensional representations inspired by semidefinite programming approaches to combinatorial optimization.

The second step matters because an otherwise useful continuous extension could create an undesirable low-dimensional bottleneck inside a neural system. Experiments in unsupervised neural combinatorial optimization show benefits from the proposed extensions, particularly when using high-dimensional representations. The contribution connects continuous treatment of set functions with representations that better fit the dimensional structure of neural architectures.
neurips-2022-neural-set-function-extensi.tldr: The paper extends discrete set functions into continuous domains and high-dimensional representations for neural combinatorial optimization.

paragraphs: NUWA-Infinity addresses visual synthesis at scales such as high-resolution images and long videos. Dividing these outputs into manageable patches makes processing possible, but independently modeling patches can lose relationships across the full image or video. The paper focuses on retaining those relationships while working one patch at a time.

Its training strategy treats an ordered sequence of non-overlapping patches as a complete instance. A rendering model predicts each patch using its available context. After a patch is predicted, optimization happens immediately, and the model saves hidden states to provide context for the next patch. This repeats as a render-and-optimize sequence.

Passing context forward provides implicit modeling of a global probability distribution, while immediate optimization is intended to reduce optimization pressure and help convergence. The authors report strong synthesis ability for high-resolution images and long-duration videos. The central contribution is a way to connect local generation steps across a larger visual output while structuring optimization around those same steps.
neurips-2022-nuwa-infinity-autoregressiv.tldr: NUWA-Infinity generates and optimizes patches sequentially while carrying context forward to support coherent large images and long videos.

paragraphs: Zero-shot coordination tests how well independently trained agents work together. This paper examines distribution shifts that can arise in that setting and in coordination with unfamiliar teammates. It focuses on off-belief learning, whose belief model can encounter inputs distributed differently from those used during learning, as can the resulting neural policy.

The first proposed method, off-team belief learning, aims to improve a target policy’s belief estimates over a broader range of inputs. It approximately reweights trajectories according to the distribution produced by a different policy. This changes which experiences influence belief learning while keeping the target policy’s belief accuracy as the objective.

The second method, off-team off-belief learning, changes how equilibrium error is weighted. It uses the distribution generated when the training policy plays with a different fixed policy, instead of the distribution from self-play. Both proposals therefore bring experience associated with another policy into learning. The authors investigate them in Hanabi variants; the abstract presents their intended mechanisms without claiming a specific performance improvement.
neurips-2022-off-team-learning-b3454383b.tldr: Off-team learning introduces two methods that account for other policies’ experience distributions when learning beliefs and coordination behavior.

paragraphs: Cardinality estimation uses a compact summary of a data stream to estimate how many distinct items it contains. This paper investigates the privacy of a broad class of such streaming algorithms. Its results show that privacy guarantees can follow from the estimators’ existing behavior, with different guarantees depending on whether a down-sampling step is added.

With simple down-sampling, the algorithms satisfy epsilon-differential privacy provided the stream’s distinct-item count is sufficiently large, scaling as k divided by epsilon. Here, k is a sketch parameter bounded by the sketch’s size in bits and typically much smaller. Both the down-sampling procedure and the cardinality condition are part of this guarantee.

Without modifying the algorithms, the authors also establish approximate differential privacy, with the delta parameter decreasing exponentially as cardinality grows. The analysis covers essentially all popular cardinality estimators and strengthens earlier privacy bounds. The proposed approach is also reported to be faster and to improve the tradeoff between estimation utility and storage space compared with prior work.
neurips-2022-order-invariant-cardinality.tldr: A broad class of cardinality estimators has privacy guarantees, including pure differential privacy with down-sampling and sufficiently large stream cardinality.

paragraphs: PKD studies how a stronger object detector can teach a compact detector even when their detection heads and label assignments differ. The authors find that a heterogeneous teacher’s feature pyramid representations can still benefit the student. However, directly forcing feature maps to match can make differences in feature magnitude unnecessarily restrictive.

Magnitude also affects which features dominate learning: large-valued stages or channels can overwhelm other information through the distillation gradient. PKD instead uses Pearson correlation to encourage the student to reproduce relationships in the teacher’s features. This relaxes magnitude matching and focuses the learning signal on how feature values vary together.

Experiments report improvements over existing detection distillation methods for both matching and differing teacher–student architectures, along with faster convergence. With a MaskRCNN-Swin teacher, ResNet-50 RetinaNet and FCOS students reach 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, respectively. These results support correlation-based feature transfer as a way to make teacher information useful across detector designs without requiring close agreement in feature scale.
neurips-2022-pkd-general-distillation-fr.tldr: PKD transfers detector features through Pearson correlation, reducing sensitivity to magnitude differences between teachers and students.

paragraphs: PointTAD detects when actions occur in untrimmed videos containing multiple action classes. This setting requires distinguishing actions within the same video and locating instances that can overlap in time. The paper extends sparse query-based detection to address these demands rather than relying on a setting dominated by one action label.

Each action instance is represented by a small collection of learnable query points corresponding to informative frames. These points can identify evidence near action boundaries as well as inside an action. A Multi-level Interactive Module then combines information at the point level and the instance level during action decoding.

The resulting model trains end to end using RGB input. The authors evaluate it on two benchmarks and introduce detection-mAP for multi-label temporal action detection. PointTAD substantially outperforms previous methods under that metric and also achieves promising segmentation-mAP results. The findings support selecting informative moments and combining their information as a useful approach to separating and locating co-occurring actions.
neurips-2022-pointtad-multi-label-tempor.tldr: PointTAD uses learnable frame queries and multi-level interaction to locate overlapping action instances in multi-label videos.

paragraphs: This paper studies entropy estimation when individual users each hold a sample and communicate with a central server. The algorithms must protect each user’s information while limiting transmitted data. The authors develop estimators for several entropy measures that all satisfy local differential privacy and have constant communication cost.

For Shannon entropy, the result concerns joint distributions whose conditional independence graph is a tree. Under that structural assumption, the required sample count grows linearly with the number of variables, improving on earlier quadratic dependence. For Gini entropy, the proposed estimator’s sample complexity does not depend on how many possible outcomes the distribution has.

The Gini estimator also needs only one concurrent communication round, whereas the previously best-known approach required costly communication and server-facilitated interaction between users. For collision entropy, the authors preserve the best-known space and sample complexity while adding privacy and communication efficiency. These are complementary results: one exploits tree structure, another removes support-size dependence, and another extends an existing efficiency guarantee to private distributed estimation.
neurips-2022-private-and-communication-e.tldr: The paper develops locally private entropy estimators with constant communication cost and improved or preserved sample-complexity guarantees.

paragraphs: Support Decomposition Variational Inference addresses probabilistic programs whose possible random-variable configurations depend on stochastic execution. This makes designing an approximation to the program’s distribution difficult: the approximation must accommodate the program’s changing support. The paper focuses on how to organize that approximation rather than keeping one global construction for the entire program.

Existing approaches build a single variational guide variable by variable while retaining the original stochastic control flow. SDVI instead decomposes the program into sub-programs with static support. It then automatically constructs a separate sub-guide for each. Within each component, the support no longer changes, simplifying the task of choosing a suitable family of approximate distributions.

The authors report that this decomposition substantially improves inference performance by making suitable variational families easier to construct. The key contribution is the change in the unit of inference design: separately modeled static-support pieces replace a single guide that must accommodate all the program’s stochastic structure. This directly connects program organization to the quality of its approximate inference.
neurips-2022-rethinking-variational-infe.tldr: SDVI improves inference for stochastic-support programs by decomposing them into static-support pieces with separately constructed variational guides.

paragraphs: Group testing seeks a small hidden subset within a much larger collection by querying groups of elements. This paper studies quantitative group testing, where each answer gives the number of hidden elements inside the queried group. The objective is to construct informative queries and recover every possible hidden subset efficiently.

The proposed algorithms are deterministic and non-adaptive: they use no random choices, and all queries can be specified without waiting for earlier answers. This avoids dependence on randomized outcomes and removes the sequential dependency of adaptive query construction. The contribution covers both building the query set and decoding the hidden subset from the resulting counts.

The authors claim the first algorithms for this setting that combine polynomial-time computation with scalability measured by a polylogarithmic number of queries per hidden element. These requirements distinguish an executable construction from a proof that a suitable query set merely exists. The result brings computational efficiency, controlled query growth, and deterministic recovery together under the quantitative-answer model.
neurips-2022-scalable-and-efficient-non-.tldr: The paper gives efficient deterministic quantitative group-testing algorithms whose queries are fixed in advance and scale polylogarithmically per hidden element.

paragraphs: SoftPatch studies image anomaly detection when training data contains label-level noise. This matters because methods evaluated with clean training collections can struggle when their data is contaminated. The paper develops a memory-based unsupervised detector that deals with noise at the patch level while retaining a useful model of normal appearance.

Noise discriminators assign outlier scores to image patches before the method constructs its coreset, a selected collection used by the memory-based detector. Those scores support removal of noisy patches. The method also stores the scores in its memory bank, using them to soften the anomaly detection boundary rather than treating the selected examples with excessive confidence.

The authors report that this combination preserves strong normal-data modeling while reducing overconfidence associated with the coreset. Across several noise scenarios, SoftPatch outperforms state-of-the-art anomaly detectors on MVTecAD and BTAD. Under clean-data conditions, its performance is comparable to those methods. The results support handling contamination explicitly within memory construction and subsequent anomaly decisions.
neurips-2022-softpatch-unsupervised-anom.tldr: SoftPatch uses patch-level outlier scores to clean anomaly-detection memory and reduce overconfidence when training data is noisy.

paragraphs: Neural Sewing Machine represents 3D garments through their sewing patterns. The motivation is that a pattern describes the garment’s underlying structure and topology, allowing the representation to accommodate diverse garment forms. The framework supports both reconstructing clothing from images and controllably changing its category, shape, or topology.

A unified encoder converts the sewing pattern into an embedding. A garment decoder then turns that embedding into a 3D garment using masked UV-position maps. Training includes separate losses for preserving structure within panels and between panels, together with a surface-normal loss. These objectives explicitly connect the predicted geometry to the garment’s panel structure.

The authors evaluate the framework on a public garment dataset containing sewing patterns and varied garment categories and shapes. They report realistic image-based reconstruction, accurate controlled manipulation, and clear improvements over state-of-the-art methods. The stated results support sewing patterns as a useful representation for combining structural preservation with variation across garment types, rather than limiting modeling to a narrow category or simple topology.
neurips-2022-structure-preserving-3d-gar.tldr: Neural Sewing Machine encodes sewing patterns to reconstruct and manipulate diverse 3D garments while preserving their panel structure.

paragraphs: Reward shaping changes the learning signals supplied to a reinforcement learning agent. Although practical systems often depend heavily on reward engineering, its effect on the amount of experience needed to learn has received less formal treatment. This paper examines why particular shaping choices can reduce that sample requirement.

The authors build on novelty-based exploration to introduce a simple way to incorporate shaped rewards. They also develop an analysis tool that proves sample-efficiency improvements for particular choices of shaping. The guarantees are selective: the paper characterizes a class of problems where substantial gains are expected, rather than claiming that any modified reward will help.

The analysis connects these ideas to practical algorithms, and experiments support the predicted benefits. The reported improvement concerns learning more efficiently while retaining asymptotic performance, so the role of shaping is to improve the learning process without sacrificing its eventual performance in the studied setting. The work provides a formal account of mechanisms behind a technique widely used in practice.
neurips-2022-unpacking-reward-shaping-un.tldr: The paper shows how particular reward-shaping choices can provably reduce reinforcement learning sample needs while retaining asymptotic performance.

paragraphs: TARGET-VAE learns object representations that separate what an object is from where it appears and how it is rotated. The motivating observation is that changes in location and pose need not change an object’s semantic identity. The method seeks this separation without supervision, including when the training images contain substantial pose and location variation.

The framework combines three coordinated components. Its encoder is equivariant to translation and rotation, meaning its behavior follows those transformations in a structured way. Its latent distribution explicitly separates rotation, translation, and semantic information, which are inferred jointly. A spatially equivariant generator completes the model, keeping transformation structure involved in reconstruction as well as inference.

Experiments report improved disentanglement and avoidance of pathologies found in earlier methods. Semantic representations learned from strongly translated and rotated images resemble those learned from consistently posed objects, substantially improving clustering. The method also achieves accurate unsupervised pose and location inference. These findings support encoding transformation structure throughout the model to keep semantic grouping distinct from spatial variation.
neurips-2022-unsupervised-object-represe.tldr: TARGET-VAE uses transformation-aware architecture and separated latent variables to learn object semantics, pose, and location without supervision.

paragraphs: Local training reduces communication in distributed optimization by allowing clients to perform more gradient-based work before averaging parameters. This is central to federated learning, but reducing communication does not by itself establish faster overall training. The paper examines local computation cost alongside communication, building on the accelerated local-training method ProxSkip.

The authors add variance reduction to ProxSkip and analyze total training time. Their key result is conditional: the new method can be substantially faster when local computation is sufficiently expensive. They characterize that threshold theoretically, making explicit when the additional algorithmic machinery can improve the combined cost of computation and communication.

Empirical results and carefully engineered proof-of-concept experiments support the theoretical predictions. The treatment of variance reduction is generic enough to accommodate many techniques, suggesting scope for additional applications. The contribution is both an enhancement to accelerated local training and a broader accounting of efficiency: it evaluates the work clients perform as well as the number of times they exchange parameters.
neurips-2022-variance-reduced-proxskip-a.tldr: Variance-reduced ProxSkip can improve total training time when local computation is sufficiently costly, with theory identifying the relevant threshold.
